newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli settlers demolishing Arab house in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli settlers demolishing Arab house in Hebron.

text.p: Jewish settlers on Friday began demolishing an Arab house in Hebron confiscated by Israeli military authorities in 1979, Palestinians said.
They said about 10 settlers were drilling through the ceiling of the house, located near a Jewish enclave in the Israeli-held part of Hebron.

"They are using large drills to demolish the roof," Suleiman Abu Snaineh, a member of the Palestinian Legislative Council, told Reuters. "The settlers are acting arrogantly and in direct challenge to the peace approach."

Jamal al-Hamouz, whose family owns the house, said Israeli military authorities confiscated the building in 1979 claiming it had been built on land that belonged to Jews before the establishment of Israel in 1948.
He said Israel changed the reason when the family appealed the confiscation, saying the building was needed for military use.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to the Palestine Liberation Organisation last month under a U.S.-brokered interim peace accord. But the heart of the town, where some 400 Jewish settlers live or study amid some 20,000 Palestinians, is under Israeli control.
Settlers say they intend to build a 10-unit apartment complex in Hebron and have been clearing rubble from the area of the Hamouze building and an adjacent lot for more than a month.

But an Israeli army spokesman said the settlers had no permit to build. He said the army stopped the settlers when they readied to build after cleaning the area but had no information on any demolition work.
